security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown code fences, package installation examples, OAuth configuration, localhost development URLs, and documentation links. No prompt injection or malicious exfiltration intent was found in SKILL.md. One semantic issue remains: the sample error handler sends raw exception messages back to the conversation.

remediation.issue: The sample error handler returns exception.Message to the user.
remediation.suggestion: Log detailed exceptions server-side and send a generic error message to the user.

semantic_findings.title: Raw Exception Message Exposed to User
semantic_findings.description: The OnTurnErrorAsync sample assigns exception.Message to an outgoing end-of-conversation activity. Production agents should avoid exposing internal error details to chat users.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code directly copies Exception.Message into an outbound activity after an error. This is a secure coding issue in sample code, not evidence of malicious intent.

content.value_statement: Building Microsoft 365 agents in .NET requires coordinated hosting, routing, authentication, and Copilot Studio setup. This skill gives focused patterns and prompts for building those pieces faster.
actual_capabilities: Lists the Microsoft.Agents NuGet packages used for hosting, authentication, storage, and Copilot Studio clients.
Shows an appsettings pattern for token validation, service connections, and Copilot Studio client settings.
Demonstrates an ASP.NET Core agent host with authentication, authorization, and message routing.
Explains AgentApplication handlers for welcome events, message activity, and turn errors.
Shows MSAL token acquisition for a Copilot Studio direct-to-engine client.
Links official Microsoft documentation and sample repositories for deeper validation.
limitations: Does not verify current NuGet versions automatically.
Uses MemoryStorage only as a development example.
Requires Microsoft tenant, app registration, and agent channel setup outside the skill.
Shows placeholder secrets and expects secure production configuration.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Basic Agent Host
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the m365-agents-dotnet skill to outline an ASP.NET Core host for a Microsoft 365 agent. Include packages, routes, auth, and storage choices.

prompt_templates.title: Design Agent Routing
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the skill to plan AgentApplication handlers for welcome events, message replies, and errors. Explain where each handler belongs.

prompt_templates.title: Configure Production Authentication
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the skill to review my Microsoft 365 agent authentication plan. Check token validation, tenant settings, authorization, and secret handling.

prompt_templates.title: Integrate Copilot Studio Client
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the skill to design a Copilot Studio direct-to-engine client. Include MSAL flow, HttpClientFactory usage, and production hardening questions.

output_examples.input: Plan a new Microsoft 365 agent host in ASP.NET Core.
output_examples.output: A concise implementation plan with package choices, host startup steps, endpoint routing, storage notes, and authentication checkpoints.

output_examples.input: Review my Teams agent authentication design.
output_examples.output: A security review covering token validation, tenant configuration, endpoint authorization, secret storage, and production readiness gaps.

output_examples.input: Help connect a .NET app to Copilot Studio.
output_examples.output: A client design summary covering MSAL token flow, connection settings, HttpClientFactory usage, and validation questions.

best_practices: Verify current Microsoft.Agents APIs and NuGet versions before implementation.
Use durable storage and secure secret providers for production agents.
Require authorization on message endpoints and validate tokens in production.
anti_patterns: Do not use MemoryStorage for production conversation state.
Do not return raw exception details to users.
Do not hardcode tenant secrets or client secrets in source files.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps build Microsoft 365 agents with .NET, ASP.NET Core hosting, AgentApplication routing, and Microsoft authentication patterns.

faq.question: Does it create a complete production app?
faq.answer: No. It provides implementation patterns and prompts, but production deployment still needs tenant setup, app registration, storage, and operations work.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks the skill as compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it cover Copilot Studio?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a direct-to-engine client pattern with MSAL token acquisition and HttpClientFactory usage.

faq.question: Does it manage Microsoft credentials?
faq.answer: No. It uses placeholders and expects secure credential management through approved configuration providers.

faq.question: Should I verify Microsoft documentation?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill explicitly recommends checking current Microsoft documentation and NuGet versions before implementation.
